data.standardized_narrative: The Syndicate reported a significant gross release of GBP 77.022m in prior year reserves for 2017. This favorable development was primarily driven by positive reserve movements on the 2014 and prior years of account, and to a lesser extent the 2015 year of account, particularly within Property and Aviation reserves. The 2015 year of account closed with a profit, reflecting robust reserves and positive claims development. However, the 2016 year of account experienced adverse development from specific events, including Hurricane Matthew (2016) and the 2017 hurricanes (Harvey, Irma, Maria) which were partly attributable to the 2016 YOA, but these were more than offset by releases from older years. The prior year movement also reflects changes in IBNR and reinsurance recoveries, as well as the impact of the Reinsurance to Close (RITC) process for the 2015 year of account.
raw_causal_phrases: positive reserve movements in the year, particularly on the 2014 and prior years of account, and to a lesser extent 2015. These have mostly been on Property reserves but also on Aviation

improvement of GBP 10.8m on closed year reserves, which makes up the largest proportion of the result. The reserves set on the 2015 pure year of account at the end of last year have also proved robust, and we have experienced positive claims development

Favourable movements of GBP 14.4 million, (2016: GBP 22.2 million), in the past year's provision for claims outstanding and IBNR, net of expected reinsurance recoveries, are included in claims incurred, net of reinsurance

YoA 2016 was battered by Hurricane Matthew, which was the most severe loss of the 2016 North Atlantic windstorm season (estimated to cost the Syndicate US$ 27.5m), as well as by the three Hurricanes of the 2017 windstorm season: Harvey, Irma and Maria (estimated gross loss US$32m attributable to YoA 2016)

data.data_quality_notes: The gross prior year development figure is taken from the 'Change in prior year provisions' in Note 17, which is a direct reconciliation of technical provisions. This figure is significantly different from a calculation based on the claims development triangle, likely due to the Reinsurance to Close (RITC) of the 2015 year of account at 31 December 2017, which can distort triangle-based PYD calculations. The gross prior year development is not broken down by line of business in the report. Net favorable movements for Property and Aviation were mentioned for 2014/2015 years of account.
